SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair

pliers noun

also pincers, tongs

classical

forceps, forcipis m./f.

noun, third declension

tongs or pincers

The strongest ancient basis for ordinary modern pliers.

Other words

  • flexibulum, -ī n. — pliers, pincers

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. pliers / pincers, citing Kirsch and Helfer

    Neo-Latin; not in Lewis & Short. It is not presented as ancient Latin.

  • forceps ad clāvōs ēvellendōs — nail-pulling pincers

    also used · our formation

    This complete phrase is our description, specifying the purpose of the curved-jaw tool photographed on site. The same broad noun forceps covers ordinary gripping pliers.

  • forfex, forficis f. — shears, scissors

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical

    Primarily denotes shears or scissors in ancient usage. It does occur as one later proposal for a wrench, but we do not use it as our generic word for pliers.

Examples

  • Forcipem mihi dā.

    Give me the pliers.composed

  • Forcipe tene.

    Hold it with the pliers.composed

See also shears, wrench.

SourcesLewis & Short: forceps · Lewis & Short: forfex · Morgan–Owens: pliers / pincers · Morgan–Owens: wrench

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
